definition: Sequential means following in a fixed order, one after another.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sequential. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sequential should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Karate ranks are sequential; no student tests for brown until green is earned.
An ordered shelf has a place for everything; sequential adds that the places must be taken one after another, in line.
Lockstep goes past sequential — not only must the steps come in order, nothing may drift even a beat out of pace.

Consecutive counts pure adjacency: things back-to-back with nothing between, like three consecutive wins or five consecutive seats. It says nothing about a required order. Sequential adds the requirement — the stages must come in that order, each unlocked by the last.

Step-by-step describes a process taken one stage at a time, and it is the friendly, instruction-manual way to say so — a recipe, a tutorial, a patient teacher walking someone through. It makes no claim that the order is required. Sequential makes exactly that claim: skip a stage, or swap two, and the process breaks.

The flight is strictly sequential.
